domain: Each primary or resource that can contain references gets its own primary-key/name/SHA capture. A single main-file binding list cannot establish transitive closure.

recursive.enumeration: Independently discover every node from captured immutable bytes under a frozen reference rule. Each file has exactly one byte identity and parsed/reference-free rule digest. Every file reachable from the root, no orphan or invented referenced node, and every required reference has exactly one typed graph edge.
recursive.context: A nested IMPORT_STRUCTURE resolves relative to the nested file directory under the existing authenticated root; never reuse the outer directory as its base. Logical keys retain each spelling/owner edge even when hashes match. Source-pair files can be shared without deduplicating semantic owners.
recursive.cycles: Cycle detection applies to recursive decoder invocations, not every source association. Recursive structure-import cycles reject completeLoaded/Save with E_GRAPH_CYCLE, retain raw graph for readonly recovery. Finite GAMESS pair back-links are nonrecursive associations and do not by themselves imply an infinite decoder call.
recursive.limits: Use captured host/model limits for node count, bytes, nesting and work before allocation. Exhaustion is a diagnostic failure preserving old draft, not partial success. No fixed research example cap is a promised native limit.
recursive.referenceFree: Only a trusted independently selected format rule can mark a resource reference-free. Client flags, file extension alone, empty supplied references, and opaque bytes cannot certify closure.

optional.probe: An applicable exact optional-name rule must appear once even when absent. The authenticated host capture snapshot binds the attempted logical sibling name and outcome. Presence requires the actual bytes/SHA/length, derived reference and effect; absence is a snapshot fact, not a permanent filesystem promise or client boolean.
optional.changed: Present-to-absent, absent-to-present, changed source bytes or rules require a new capture/baseline and plan. This is an explicit refresh/import, not hidden live data replacement on unrelated edit or Saved acknowledgment.
optional.reopen: Artifact-only portable reopen uses the captured optional outcome and explicit graph, never ambient CWD/sibling/cache fallback. An absent optional companion contributes no invented object; a present one must satisfy its own content/owner expectation. Existing D2-13 filesystem check/use limitation remains.
optional.failure: Required explicit references cannot downgrade to optional. A malformed/unreadable/denied existing companion is diagnostic, not certified absent. Recovery may expose raw resources without claiming full reconstructed geometry.

rietan.selectedNames: For selected .ins/.lst source names, replace the last extension with literal .ffe in the same captured directory; preserve case and all prefix bytes. Lowercase suffix subset is selected in finite model; no arbitrary encoding/path normalization.
rietan.native: Locked RIETAN input and LST readers construct a phase-owned path at +0x830 by copying the primary path through its last dot and appending .ffe. Manual17.6.1 confirms optional load and its geometrical-parameter table effect.
rietan.producer: Manual16.2/cooperation2.9 describe RIETAN-FP writing updated .vesta/Cycle/Iter files. This is producer filesystem activity, not evidence of VESTA scanning .ins on ordinary .vesta reopen. Preserve such bytes as captured source; do not create an unproved implicit input edge.
rietan.effect: Present .ffe binds source-ordered distance/angle rows, pair/triplet symmetry/site identities and units/SU where qualified. It does not run ORFFE, recompute geometry, or grant unqualified site association; missing identity stays source-table/diagnostic. Explicit IMPORT_ORFFE is required once recorded and cannot be silently ignored.

integration.save: Register full transitive reference graph and optional outcomes with the immutable SaveExpectation. Build candidate/persisted artifact-only contexts from this graph; missing a nested node or a present optional table is E_REOPEN_REFERENCE/COVERAGE even if every listed SHA matches.
integration.sourceAndActive: Resource capture/source preservation and active semantic reconstruction remain distinct. A preserved but unqualified table does not count as reconstructed geometry, just as byte-correct pgrid does not count as a Field.
integration.protocol: New standalone internal graph proposal extends existing single-file capture by composition; original capture URI/protocol3 remain unchanged. Any transported graph requires separately versioned admission.

cumulativeParseBudget: parse-budget.contract.json: cumulative authenticated per-job limits across all nested resources/source trees/decoded buffers, stored samples and semantic references; checked counts before allocation, no child reset or partial install. Decode budget failure is failed-before-apply, not an invalid scientific source verdict. Candidate/persisted verification uses its own registered limits under the same source/artifact identities; actual04 quotas remain separate.
producerIncludes: feff10-source.contract.json: selected producer include/load are recursive inline source expansion, distinct from structure-import and nonrecursive producer-pair. Exact source job-base/captured virtual name map and invocation order must qualify; no ambient CWD or assumed declaring-file-parent fallback.
migration: Internal graph1->graph2 successor adds producer-include with mandatory recursiveDecode=true. Exact schema/rule/source context digests and a fresh authenticated complete capture are required; never silently reuse old policyDigest/plan/consent or infer graph2 semantics from a client edge. Productprotocol3 and old graph1 snapshots remain unchanged; transport admission remains separately versioned.

boundDescriptorContexts.scope: Exact immutable descriptor bytes plus owner/use-scoped typed fresh reference contexts; complete native-path and typed-resource closure are separate domains, no raw-alias fallback or science admission.
